# Implement Plan

You are tasked with implementing an approved technical plan from `thoughts/shared/plans/`. These plans contain phases with specific changes and success criteria.

## Getting Started

When given a plan path:
- Read the plan completely and check for any existing checkmarks (- [x])
- Read the original ticket and all files mentioned in the plan
- **Read files fully** - never use limit/offset parameters, you need complete context
- Think deeply about how the pieces fit together
- Create a todo list to track your progress
- Start implementing if you understand what needs to be done

If no plan path provided, ask for one.

## Implementation Philosophy

Plans are carefully designed, but reality can be messy. Your job is to:
- Follow the plan's intent while adapting to what you find
- Implement each phase fully before moving to the next
- Verify your work makes sense in the broader codebase context
- Update checkboxes in the plan as you complete sections

When things don't match the plan exactly, think about why and communicate clearly. The plan is your guide, but your judgment matters too.

If you encounter a mismatch:
- STOP and think deeply about why the plan can't be followed
- Present the issue clearly:
  ```
  Issue in Phase [N]:
  Expected: [what the plan says]
  Found: [actual situation]
  Why this matters: [explanation]

  How should I proceed?
  ```

## Verification Approach

After implementing a phase:
- Run the success criteria checks (usually `make check test` covers everything)
- Fix any issues before proceeding
- Update your progress in both the plan and your todos
- Check off completed items in the plan file itself using Edit
- **Pause for human verification**: After completing all automated verification for a phase, pause and inform the human that the phase is ready for manual testing. Use this format:
  ```
  Phase [N] Complete - Ready for Manual Verification

  Automated verification passed:
  - [List automated checks that passed]

  Please perform the manual verification steps listed in the plan:
  - [List manual verification items from the plan]

  Let me know when manual testing is complete so I can proceed to Phase [N+1].
  ```

If instructed to execute multiple phases consecutively, skip the pause until the last phase. Otherwise, assume you are just doing one phase.

do not check off items in the manual testing steps until confirmed by the user.


## If You Get Stuck

When something isn't working as expected:
- First, make sure you've read and understood all the relevant code
- Consider if the codebase has evolved since the plan was written
- Present the mismatch clearly and ask for guidance

Use sub-tasks sparingly - mainly for targeted debugging or exploring unfamiliar territory.

## Resuming Work

If the plan has existing checkmarks:
- Trust that completed work is done
- Pick up from the first unchecked item
- Verify previous work only if something seems off

Remember: You're implementing a solution, not just checking boxes. Keep the end goal in mind and maintain forward momentum.

input.title: Add devcontainer.json fallback config reader
input.description:
Add `devcontainer.json` as a fallback configuration source when no `.dual.toml` exists. This gives Dual zero-config compatibility with the ~15% of repos that already have `.devcontainer/` directories, while keeping `.dual.toml` as the primary config.

## Changes

- **New `src/devcontainer.rs` module** — Parser for devcontainer.json with support for `image`, `build`, `forwardPorts`, `containerEnv`, `postCreateCommand`, and `mounts` fields. Handles all spec-allowed format variants (string/array/object commands, integer/string ports, string/object mounts).
- **Config fallback chain** — `load_hints()` now checks: `.dual.toml` → `devcontainer.json` → defaults. `.dual.toml` always takes priority.
- **Docker build support** — New `build_image()` / `build_image_args()` in `container.rs` to handle `build.dockerfile` from devcontainer.json. `cmd_launch()` builds the image before creating the container when configured.
- **`DockerfileBuild` struct** — Added to `config.rs` with path, context, args, target, and base_dir fields.

## Out of Scope

- Dev container features (OCI artifacts)
- Lifecycle hooks beyond `postCreateCommand`
- Variable substitution (`${localEnv:VAR}`)
- Docker Compose / `dockerComposeFile`
- IDE customizations

## Testing

- 25 unit tests for devcontainer parser (all format variants)
- 5 unit tests for `build_image_args` construction
- Full integration verified through `load_hints()` fallback chain

# Dual

Terminal workspace orchestrator for parallel multi-repo development with AI coding agents.

Dual manages isolated development environments — one full git clone per workspace, one Docker container per clone — so you can run multiple repos on multiple branches simultaneously, all with Claude Code sessions active, all running dev servers on default ports, with zero conflicts.

## Installation

**curl (macOS/Linux):**

```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/jeevanpillay/dual/releases/latest/download/dual-installer.sh | sh
```

**PowerShell (Windows):**

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://github.com/jeevanpillay/dual/releases/latest/download/dual-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

**From source:**

```bash
cargo install --path .
```

## Prerequisites

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
- [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux)

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Register your repo
cd ~/code/my-project
dual add

# 2. Create a branch workspace
dual create feat/auth

# 3. Launch the TUI and select a workspace
dual
```

`dual` opens an interactive workspace browser. Select a workspace to launch it — Dual clones the repo, starts a Docker container, sets up transparent command routing, and drops you into a tmux session. Detach from tmux (`Ctrl+b d`) and you're back in the browser.

## The TUI

Running `dual` with no arguments opens the workspace browser:

```
 dual  workspace browser
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│▼ my-project                          │
│  main                     ● running  │
│  feat/auth                ○ stopped  │
│  feat/billing             ◌ lazy     │
│▼ agent-os                            │
│  main                     ● running  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
 j/k navigate  enter launch  q quit
```

- **j/k** or arrow keys to navigate
- **Enter** on a workspace to launch it (clone + container + tmux)
- **Enter** on a repo header to expand/collapse
- **q** or Esc to quit

When you select a workspace, the TUI suspends, tmux takes over. Detach from tmux (`Ctrl+b d`) and the TUI resumes automatically with fresh status.

### Tmux keybinding

For quick access from any tmux session, add to `~/.tmux.conf`:

```bash
# Prefix + Space to open Dual picker in a popup
bind-key Space display-popup -E -w 60% -h 60% "dual"

# Or without prefix — Alt+Space (Meta+Space)
# bind-key -n M-Space display-popup -E -w 60% -h 60% "dual"
```

`Prefix + Space` opens the Dual picker in a popup overlay. Select a workspace and the popup disappears as tmux switches to it.

## CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `dual` | Open TUI workspace browser |
| `dual add [--name NAME]` | Register current git repo as a workspace |
| `dual create <branch> [--repo NAME]` | Create a new branch workspace |
| `dual launch [workspace]` | Launch a workspace (auto-detects from cwd) |
| `dual list` | List all workspaces with status (non-interactive) |
| `dual destroy [workspace]` | Tear down workspace (container, tmux, clone) |
| `dual open [workspace]` | Open workspace services in browser |
| `dual urls [workspace]` | Display workspace URLs |
| `dual sync [workspace]` | Sync shared config files across branch workspaces |
| `dual proxy` | Start reverse proxy for browser access |

## Configuration

Dual uses two config files:

### `.dual.toml` (per-repo hints)

Lives in your project root. Committed to git. Controls runtime behavior.

```toml
# Docker image for the container runtime
image = "node:20"

# Ports your dev server uses (for reverse proxy routing)
ports = [3000, 3001]

# Shell command to run after container creation (e.g., dependency install)
setup = "pnpm install"

# Commands to route to the container (in addition to defaults)
# Default: npm, npx, pnpm, node, python, python3, pip, pip3, curl, make
extra_commands = ["cargo", "go"]

# Directories to isolate with anonymous Docker volumes
anonymous_volumes = ["node_modules", ".next"]

# Environment variables passed to the container
[env]
NODE_ENV = "development"

# Files to share across all workspaces of this repo
[shared]
files = [".vercel", ".env.local"]
```

| Field | Description | Default |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `image` | Docker image for the container | `node:20` |
| `ports` | Ports that services bind to (for reverse proxy) | `[]` |
| `setup` | Command to run after first container creation | None |
| `env` | Environment variables passed to the container | `{}` |
| `shared.files` | Files/directories to share across branch workspaces | `[]` |
| `extra_commands` | Additional commands to route to the container | `[]` |
| `anonymous_volumes` | Container volumes (e.g., `node_modules`) | `["node_modules"]` |

### `~/.dual/workspaces.toml` (global state)

Managed by Dual. Tracks all registered workspaces.

```toml
workspace_root = "~/dual-workspaces"

[[workspaces]]
repo = "my-project"
url = "git@github.com:org/my-project.git"
branch = "main"
path = "/Users/you/code/my-project"

[[workspaces]]
repo = "my-project"
url = "git@github.com:org/my-project.git"
branch = "feat/auth"
```

## How It Works

When you select a workspace (via `dual` or `dual launch`):

1. **Clone** — Clones the repo into `{workspace_root}/{repo}/{branch}/` (uses `git clone --local` from main workspace for speed)
2. **Shared files** — Copies shared config files (`.env.local`, `.vercel`, etc.) from `~/.dual/shared/{repo}/`
3. **Container** — Creates and starts a Docker container with the clone bind-mounted
4. **Setup** — Runs `setup` command on first launch (e.g., `pnpm install`)
5. **Shell RC** — Generates transparent command routing that intercepts runtime commands and routes them to the container via `docker exec`
6. **Tmux** — Creates a tmux session in the workspace directory and attaches

Your editor, git, and credentials stay on the host. The container handles all runtime processes. Claude Code never knows it's running inside a container.

## Architecture

```
Terminal
├── State A: Dual TUI (ratatui)
│   └── Select workspace → suspend TUI → launch pipeline → tmux attach
└── State B: tmux session
    └── Detach (Ctrl+b d) → resume TUI

Host                          Container
+--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
| nvim, git, claude, ssh   |  | pnpm, node, python       |
| file reads/writes        |  | curl localhost, tests    |
| credentials, SSH keys    |  | port-binding processes   |
+--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
        |    bind mount    |
        +------------------+

Browser --> {repo}-{branch}.localhost:{port}
        --> reverse proxy
        --> container
```

| Host | Container |
|------|-----------|
| git, cat, ls, vim | npm, pnpm, node, python |
| File reads/writes | Port-binding processes |
| SSH, credentials | curl localhost, tests |

## Development

```bash
cargo build              # Build debug binary
cargo build --release    # Build release binary
cargo test               # Run tests (~150 tests)
cargo clippy             # Run linter
cargo fmt                # Format code
```

Targets: Linux, macOS (Intel + Apple Silicon), Windows.

## License

MIT

1→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
     2→use std::collections::HashMap;
     3→use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
     4→
     5→/// Dockerfile build configuration for building images from source.
     6→/// Used when devcontainer.json specifies `build.dockerfile` or when
     7→/// configured directly in .dual.toml.
     8→#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Clone)]
     9→pub struct DockerfileBuild {
    10→    /// Path to the Dockerfile (relative to base_dir or workspace root)
    11→    pub path: String,
    12→
    13→    /// Build context directory (relative to base_dir or workspace root)
    14→    #[serde(default = "default_build_context")]
    15→    pub context: String,
    16→
    17→    /// Docker build arguments (--build-arg)
    18→    #[serde(default)]
    19→    pub args: HashMap<String, String>,
    20→
    21→    /// Target build stage for multi-stage builds
    22→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    23→    pub target: Option<String>,
    24→
    25→    /// Base directory for resolving relative paths (set by devcontainer loader).
    26→    /// When loaded from .dual.toml, this is None and paths are relative to workspace root.
    27→    #[serde(skip)]
    28→    pub base_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    29→}
    30→
    31→fn default_build_context() -> String {
    32→    ".".to_string()
    33→}
    34→
    35→const HINTS_FILENAME: &str = ".dual.toml";
    36→const DEFAULT_IMAGE: &str = "node:20";
    37→
    38→/// Shared configuration file propagation settings.
    39→#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Clone)]
    40→pub struct SharedConfig {
    41→    /// Files and directories to share across workspaces.
    42→    /// e.g. [".vercel", ".env.local", ".env"]
    43→    #[serde(default)]
    44→    pub files: Vec<String>,
    45→}
    46→
    47→/// Per-repo runtime hints, read from .dual.toml in a workspace directory.
    48→#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Clone)]
    49→pub struct RepoHints {
    50→    /// Docker image to use for containers (default: "node:20")
    51→    #[serde(default = "default_image")]
    52→    pub image: String,
    53→
    54→    /// Ports that services bind to inside the container
    55→    #[serde(default)]
    56→    pub ports: Vec<u16>,
    57→
    58→    /// Setup command to run after container creation (e.g. "pnpm install")
    59→    pub setup: Option<String>,
    60→
    61→    /// Environment variables for the container
    62→    #[serde(default)]
    63→    pub env: HashMap<String, String>,
    64→
    65→    /// Additional commands to route to the container (merged with defaults)
    66→    #[serde(default)]
    67→    pub extra_commands: Vec<String>,
    68→
    69→    /// Directories to isolate with anonymous Docker volumes
    70→    #[serde(default = "default_anonymous_volumes")]
    71→    pub anonymous_volumes: Vec<String>,
    72→
    73→    /// Shared files to propagate across workspaces
    74→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    75→    pub shared: Option<SharedConfig>,
    76→
    77→    /// Dockerfile build config — if set, build image instead of pulling.
    78→    /// Can be set via .dual.toml [dockerfile] section or from devcontainer.json build field.
    79→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    80→    pub dockerfile: Option<DockerfileBuild>,
    81→}
    82→
    83→fn default_image() -> String {
    84→    DEFAULT_IMAGE.to_string()
    85→}
    86→
    87→fn default_anonymous_volumes() -> Vec<String> {
    88→    vec!["node_modules".to_string()]
    89→}
    90→
    91→impl Default for RepoHints {
    92→    fn default() -> Self {
    93→        Self {
    94→            image: DEFAULT_IMAGE.to_string(),
    95→            ports: Vec::new(),
    96→            setup: None,
    97→            env: HashMap::new(),
    98→            extra_commands: Vec::new(),
    99→            anonymous_volumes: default_anonymous_volumes(),
   100→            shared: None,
   101→            dockerfile: None,
   102→        }
   103→    }
   104→}
   105→
   106→/// Get the shared config directory for a repo: ~/.dual/shared/{repo}/
   107→pub fn shared_dir(repo: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
   108→    dirs::home_dir().map(|home| home.join(".dual").join("shared").join(repo))
   109→}
   110→
   111→/// Load RepoHints from a workspace directory.
   112→///
   113→/// Priority order:
   114→/// 1. `.dual.toml` — Dual-native config (always takes priority)
   115→/// 2. `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` or `.devcontainer.json` — fallback
   116→/// 3. Default hints (node:20, no ports, etc.)
   117→pub fn load_hints(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<RepoHints, HintsError> {
   118→    let path = workspace_dir.join(HINTS_FILENAME);
   119→
   120→    // 1. .dual.toml takes priority
   121→    if path.exists() {
   122→        let contents =
   123→            std::fs::read_to_string(&path).map_err(|e| HintsError::ReadError(path.clone(), e))?;
   124→        let hints: RepoHints =
   125→            toml::from_str(&contents).map_err(|e| HintsError::ParseError(path, e))?;
   126→        return Ok(hints);
   127→    }
   128→
   129→    // 2. Fall back to devcontainer.json
   130→    if let Some(hints) = crate::devcontainer::load_devcontainer_as_hints(workspace_dir) {
   131→        return Ok(hints);
   132→    }
   133→
   134→    // 3. Default
   135→    Ok(RepoHints::default())
   136→}
   137→
   138→/// Write RepoHints to a workspace directory's .dual.toml.
   139→pub fn write_hints(workspace_dir: &Path, hints: &RepoHints) -> Result<(), HintsError> {
   140→    let path = workspace_dir.join(HINTS_FILENAME);
   141→    let contents = toml::to_string_pretty(hints).map_err(HintsError::SerializeError)?;
   142→    std::fs::write(&path, contents).map_err(|e| HintsError::WriteError(path, e))?;
   143→    Ok(())
   144→}
   145→
   146→/// Write a default .dual.toml with helpful comments and examples.
   147→/// Used by `dual add` when creating a new repo config.
   148→pub fn write_default_hints(repo_root: &Path) -> Result<(), HintsError> {
   149→    let template = r#"# Dual workspace configuration
   150→# See: https://github.com/jeevanpillay/dual
   151→
   152→# Docker image for the container runtime
   153→image = "node:20"
   154→
   155→# Ports your dev server uses (for reverse proxy routing)
   156→# Example: ports = [3000, 3001]
   157→# ports = []
   158→
   159→# Shell command to run after container creation (e.g., dependency install)
   160→# Example: setup = "pnpm install"
   161→# setup = ""
   162→
   163→# Environment variables passed to the container
   164→# Example:
   165→# [env]
   166→# NODE_ENV = "development"
   167→
   168→# Commands to route to the container (in addition to defaults)
   169→# Default: npm, npx, pnpm, node, python, python3, pip, pip3, curl, make
   170→# Example: extra_commands = ["cargo", "go", "ruby"]
   171→# extra_commands = []
   172→
   173→# Directories to isolate with anonymous Docker volumes
   174→# These directories get their own volume so they don't sync between host/container
   175→# Example: anonymous_volumes = ["node_modules", ".next", "target"]
   176→# anonymous_volumes = ["node_modules"]
   177→
   178→# Files to share across all workspaces of this repo
   179→# These are gitignored files that should be available in every branch workspace
   180→# [shared]
   181→# files = [".env.local", ".vercel"]
   182→"#;
   183→    let hints_path = repo_root.join(HINTS_FILENAME);
   184→    std::fs::write(&hints_path, template).map_err(|e| HintsError::WriteError(hints_path, e))?;
   185→    Ok(())
   186→}
   187→
   188→/// Parse hints from TOML string (for testing).
   189→pub fn parse_hints(toml_str: &str) -> Result<RepoHints, HintsError> {
   190→    let hints: RepoHints = toml::from_str(toml_str)
   191→        .map_err(|e| HintsError::ParseError(PathBuf::from("<string>"), e))?;
   192→    Ok(hints)
   193→}
   194→
   195→/// Compute the workspace identifier from repo + branch.
   196→/// e.g. ("lightfast", "feat/auth") → "lightfast-feat__auth"
   197→pub fn workspace_id(repo: &str, branch: &str) -> String {
   198→    format!("{}-{}", repo, encode_branch(branch))
   199→}

Design an implementation plan for redesigning Dual's config model to make devcontainer.json the primary source for container configuration.

## Current State

Dual currently has a single config file `.dual.toml` that contains ALL fields:
- `image` (Docker image)
- `ports` (forwarded ports)
- `setup` (post-create command)
- `env` (container env vars)
- `extra_commands` (Dual-specific: commands to route to container)
- `anonymous_volumes` (Dual-specific: dirs to isolate)
- `shared` (Dual-specific: files to share across workspaces)
- `dockerfile` (just added: DockerfileBuild config)

We also just added a `devcontainer.rs` parser module that can parse devcontainer.json and convert to RepoHints. Currently it's used as a FALLBACK when no .dual.toml exists.

## Desired State

**devcontainer.json** = source of truth for container config:
- `image` or `build.dockerfile`
- `forwardPorts` (replaces `ports` in .dual.toml)
- `containerEnv` (replaces `env`)
- `postCreateCommand` (replaces `setup`)
- `mounts` (contributes to anonymous_volumes)

**`.dual.toml`** = Dual-specific concerns only:
- `devcontainer` — optional path to devcontainer.json (auto-detects .devcontainer/devcontainer.json if omitted)
- `extra_commands` — commands to route to container (not in devcontainer spec)
- `anonymous_volumes` — Dual concept for volume isolation
- `shared` — files to share across workspaces

**Removed from `.dual.toml`**: `image`, `ports`, `setup`, `env`, `dockerfile`

## Key Files and Their Current Structure

### src/config.rs
- `RepoHints` struct (lines 49-82): has all fields including image, ports, setup, env
- `load_hints()` (lines 117-136): reads .dual.toml, falls back to devcontainer, then defaults
- `write_default_hints()` (lines 148-186): creates .dual.toml template with image="node:20" etc
- `write_hints()` (lines 140-145): serializes RepoHints to TOML
- `parse_hints()` (lines 191-195): parses TOML string (for testing)
- `DockerfileBuild` struct (lines 6-33): build config
- 5 callers of load_hints(): cmd_add (main.rs:155), cmd_launch (main.rs:381), cmd_sync (main.rs:757), ProxyState::from_state (proxy.rs:56), format_workspace_urls (proxy.rs:283)

### src/devcontainer.rs
- `DevcontainerJson` struct: parsed from JSON
- `to_repo_hints()`: converts devcontainer fields to RepoHints
- `load_devcontainer_as_hints()`: find + parse + convert
- `find_devcontainer_json()`: locates .devcontainer/devcontainer.json or .devcontainer.json

### src/main.rs
- `cmd_add()` (line 146): calls write_default_hints() when no .dual.toml
- `cmd_launch()` (line 381): loads hints, uses image/env/volumes/setup/dockerfile/extra_commands
- Container creation uses: hints.image, hints.env, hints.anonymous_volumes
- Setup uses: hints.setup
- Shell RC uses: hints.extra_commands

### src/proxy.rs
- Uses hints.ports for route table (line 59) and URL display (line 286)

### tests/fixtures/mod.rs
- `create_fixture_hints()`: constructs RepoHints with all fields explicitly

### README.md
- Documents .dual.toml fields including image, ports, setup, env

## Design Considerations

1. **Internal representation**: `RepoHints` should stay as the merged internal struct (all consumers use it). But the TOML deserialization needs a NEW struct (`DualConfig`) that only has the Dual-specific fields.

2. **Loading flow**: 
   - Read .dual.toml → DualConfig (devcontainer path, extra_commands, anonymous_volumes, shared)
   - Find devcontainer.json (from DualConfig.devcontainer path or auto-detect)
   - Parse devcontainer.json → DevcontainerJson
   - Merge both into RepoHints

3. **`dual add` behavior**: Should create BOTH `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (with image: node:20) AND `.dual.toml` (with Dual-specific defaults).

4. **Backward compat**: serde ignores unknown fields by default, so old .dual.toml files with `image` etc won't error — those fields will just be silently ignored. Container config must come from devcontainer.json.

5. **No devcontainer.json**: If no devcontainer.json exists, use defaults (node:20, no ports, etc.)

Please design a phased implementation plan with specific file changes and success criteria.

1→# Dual
     2→
     3→Terminal workspace orchestrator for parallel multi-repo development with AI coding agents.
     4→
     5→Dual manages isolated development environments — one full git clone per workspace, one Docker container per clone — so you can run multiple repos on multiple branches simultaneously, all with Claude Code sessions active, all running dev servers on default ports, with zero conflicts.
     6→
     7→## Installation
     8→
     9→**curl (macOS/Linux):**
    10→
    11→```bash
    12→curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/jeevanpillay/dual/releases/latest/download/dual-installer.sh | sh
    13→```
    14→
    15→**PowerShell (Windows):**
    16→
    17→```powershell
    18→powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://github.com/jeevanpillay/dual/releases/latest/download/dual-installer.ps1 | iex"
    19→```
    20→
    21→**From source:**
    22→
    23→```bash
    24→cargo install --path .
    25→```
    26→
    27→## Prerequisites
    28→
    29→- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
    30→- [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux)
    31→
    32→## Quick Start
    33→
    34→```bash
    35→# 1. Register your repo
    36→cd ~/code/my-project
    37→dual add
    38→
    39→# 2. Create a branch workspace
    40→dual create feat/auth
    41→
    42→# 3. Launch the TUI and select a workspace
    43→dual
    44→```
    45→
    46→`dual` opens an interactive workspace browser. Select a workspace to launch it — Dual clones the repo, starts a Docker container, sets up transparent command routing, and drops you into a tmux session. Detach from tmux (`Ctrl+b d`) and you're back in the browser.
    47→
    48→## The TUI
    49→
    50→Running `dual` with no arguments opens the workspace browser:
    51→
    52→```
    53→ dual  workspace browser
    54→┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
    55→│▼ my-project                          │
    56→│  main                     ● running  │
    57→│  feat/auth                ○ stopped  │
    58→│  feat/billing             ◌ lazy     │
    59→│▼ agent-os                            │
    60→│  main                     ● running  │
    61→└──────────────────────────────────────┘
    62→ j/k navigate  enter launch  q quit
    63→```
    64→
    65→- **j/k** or arrow keys to navigate
    66→- **Enter** on a workspace to launch it (clone + container + tmux)
    67→- **Enter** on a repo header to expand/collapse
    68→- **q** or Esc to quit
    69→
    70→When you select a workspace, the TUI suspends, tmux takes over. Detach from tmux (`Ctrl+b d`) and the TUI resumes automatically with fresh status.
    71→
    72→### Tmux keybinding
    73→
    74→For quick access from any tmux session, add to `~/.tmux.conf`:
    75→
    76→```bash
    77→# Prefix + Space to open Dual picker in a popup
    78→bind-key Space display-popup -E -w 60% -h 60% "dual"
    79→
    80→# Or without prefix — Alt+Space (Meta+Space)
    81→# bind-key -n M-Space display-popup -E -w 60% -h 60% "dual"
    82→```
    83→
    84→`Prefix + Space` opens the Dual picker in a popup overlay. Select a workspace and the popup disappears as tmux switches to it.
    85→
    86→## CLI Commands
    87→
    88→| Command | Description |
    89→|---------|-------------|
    90→| `dual` | Open TUI workspace browser |
    91→| `dual add [--name NAME]` | Register current git repo as a workspace |
    92→| `dual create <branch> [--repo NAME]` | Create a new branch workspace |
    93→| `dual launch [workspace]` | Launch a workspace (auto-detects from cwd) |
    94→| `dual list` | List all workspaces with status (non-interactive) |
    95→| `dual destroy [workspace]` | Tear down workspace (container, tmux, clone) |
    96→| `dual open [workspace]` | Open workspace services in browser |
    97→| `dual urls [workspace]` | Display workspace URLs |
    98→| `dual sync [workspace]` | Sync shared config files across branch workspaces |
    99→| `dual proxy` | Start reverse proxy for browser access |
   100→
   101→## Configuration
   102→
   103→Dual uses two config files:
   104→
   105→### `.dual.toml` (per-repo hints)
   106→
   107→Lives in your project root. Committed to git. Controls runtime behavior.
   108→
   109→```toml
   110→# Docker image for the container runtime
   111→image = "node:20"
   112→
   113→# Ports your dev server uses (for reverse proxy routing)
   114→ports = [3000, 3001]
   115→
   116→# Shell command to run after container creation (e.g., dependency install)
   117→setup = "pnpm install"
   118→
   119→# Commands to route to the container (in addition to defaults)
   120→# Default: npm, npx, pnpm, node, python, python3, pip, pip3, curl, make
   121→extra_commands = ["cargo", "go"]
   122→
   123→# Directories to isolate with anonymous Docker volumes
   124→anonymous_volumes = ["node_modules", ".next"]
   125→
   126→# Environment variables passed to the container
   127→[env]
   128→NODE_ENV = "development"
   129→
   130→# Files to share across all workspaces of this repo
   131→[shared]
   132→files = [".vercel", ".env.local"]
   133→```
   134→
   135→| Field | Description | Default |
   136→|-------|-------------|---------|
   137→| `image` | Docker image for the container | `node:20` |
   138→| `ports` | Ports that services bind to (for reverse proxy) | `[]` |
   139→| `setup` | Command to run after first container creation | None |
   140→| `env` | Environment variables passed to the container | `{}` |
   141→| `shared.files` | Files/directories to share across branch workspaces | `[]` |
   142→| `extra_commands` | Additional commands to route to the container | `[]` |
   143→| `anonymous_volumes` | Container volumes (e.g., `node_modules`) | `["node_modules"]` |
   144→
   145→### `devcontainer.json` (fallback)
   146→
   147→If no `.dual.toml` exists, Dual reads `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (or `.devcontainer.json`) as a fallback. This gives zero-config compatibility with repos that already have dev container configurations.
   148→
   149→| devcontainer.json field | Maps to |
   150→|---|---|
   151→| `image` | `image` |
   152→| `build.dockerfile` | Builds image via `docker build` |
   153→| `forwardPorts` | `ports` |
   154→| `containerEnv` | `env` |
   155→| `postCreateCommand` | `setup` |
   156→| `mounts` (volume type, `/workspace/*`) | `anonymous_volumes` |
   157→
   158→`.dual.toml` always takes priority when both exist.
   159→
   160→### `~/.dual/workspaces.toml` (global state)
   161→
   162→Managed by Dual. Tracks all registered workspaces.
   163→
   164→```toml
   165→workspace_root = "~/dual-workspaces"
   166→
   167→[[workspaces]]
   168→repo = "my-project"
   169→url = "git@github.com:org/my-project.git"
   170→branch = "main"
   171→path = "/Users/you/code/my-project"
   172→
   173→[[workspaces]]
   174→repo = "my-project"
   175→url = "git@github.com:org/my-project.git"
   176→branch = "feat/auth"
   177→```
   178→
   179→## How It Works
   180→
   181→When you select a workspace (via `dual` or `dual launch`):
   182→
   183→1. **Clone** — Clones the repo into `{workspace_root}/{repo}/{branch}/` (uses `git clone --local` from main workspace for speed)
   184→2. **Shared files** — Copies shared config files (`.env.local`, `.vercel`, etc.) from `~/.dual/shared/{repo}/`
   185→3. **Container** — Creates and starts a Docker container with the clone bind-mounted
   186→4. **Setup** — Runs `setup` command on first launch (e.g., `pnpm install`)
   187→5. **Shell RC** — Generates transparent command routing that intercepts runtime commands and routes them to the container via `docker exec`
   188→6. **Tmux** — Creates a tmux session in the workspace directory and attaches
   189→
   190→Your editor, git, and credentials stay on the host. The container handles all runtime processes. Claude Code never knows it's running inside a container.
   191→
   192→### Shell Hook (Pane Propagation)
   193→
   194→`dual add` automatically appends a small snippet to your `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`:
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→# dual: shell interception (auto-generated)
   198→if [ -n "$DUAL_ACTIVE" ] && [ -n "$DUAL_RC_PATH" ] && [ -f "$DUAL_RC_PATH" ]; then
   199→    source "$DUAL_RC_PATH"
   200→fi
   201→```
   202→
   203→This ensures that when you split a pane (`Ctrl+b %`) or create a new window (`Ctrl+b c`) inside a Dual tmux session, the new shell automatically loads command interception. Without this, new panes would run commands on the host instead of in the container.
   204→
   205→The snippet is a no-op outside Dual sessions — it only activates when `DUAL_ACTIVE` is set (which Dual configures via `tmux set-environment`).
   206→
   207→## Architecture
   208→
   209→```
   210→Terminal
   211→├── State A: Dual TUI (ratatui)
   212→│   └── Select workspace → suspend TUI → launch pipeline → tmux attach
   213→└── State B: tmux session
   214→    └── Detach (Ctrl+b d) → resume TUI
   215→
   216→Host                          Container
   217→+--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
   218→| nvim, git, claude, ssh   |  | pnpm, node, python       |
   219→| file reads/writes        |  | curl localhost, tests    |
   220→| credentials, SSH keys    |  | port-binding processes   |
   221→+--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
   222→        |    bind mount    |
   223→        +------------------+
   224→
   225→Browser --> {repo}-{branch}.localhost:{port}

## Current State

Dual currently has a single config file `.dual.toml` that contains ALL fields:
- `image` (Docker image)
- `ports` (forwarded ports)
- `setup` (post-create command)
- `env` (container env vars)
- `extra_commands` (Dual-specific: commands to route to container)
- `anonymous_volumes` (Dual-specific: dirs to isolate)
- `shared` (Dual-specific: files to share across workspaces)
- `dockerfile` (just added: DockerfileBuild config)

We also just added a `devcontainer.rs` parser module that can parse devcontainer.json and convert to RepoHints. Currently it's used as a FALLBACK when no .dual.toml exists.

## Desired State

**devcontainer.json** = source of truth for container config:
- `image` or `build.dockerfile`
- `forwardPorts` (replaces `ports` in .dual.toml)
- `containerEnv` (replaces `env`)
- `postCreateCommand` (replaces `setup`)
- `mounts` (contributes to anonymous_volumes)

**`.dual.toml`** = Dual-specific concerns only:
- `devcontainer` — optional path to devcontainer.json (auto-detects .devcontainer/devcontainer.json if omitted)
- `extra_commands` — commands to route to container (not in devcontainer spec)
- `anonymous_volumes` — Dual concept for volume isolation
- `shared` — files to share across workspaces

**Removed from `.dual.toml`**: `image`, `ports`, `setup`, `env`, `dockerfile`

- `RepoHints` struct (lines 49-82): has all fields including image, ports, setup, env
- `load_hints()` (lines 117-136): reads .dual.toml, falls back to devcontainer, then defaults
- `write_default_hints()` (lines 148-186): creates .dual.toml template with image="node:20" etc

- `DevcontainerJson` struct: parsed from JSON
- `to_repo_hints()`: converts devcontainer fields to RepoHints

- `find_devcontainer_json()`: locates .devcontainer/devcontainer.json or .devcontainer.json

- `cmd_add()` (line 146): calls write_default_hints() when no .dual.toml
- `cmd_launch()` (line 381): loads hints, uses image/env/volumes/setup/dockerfile/extra_commands

- `create_fixture_hints()`: constructs RepoHints with all fields explicitly

# devcontainer.json as Primary Config Source

## Context

The current implementation treats devcontainer.json as a fallback when `.dual.toml` is missing. The user wants the opposite model: devcontainer.json is the **primary source** for container configuration, and `.dual.toml` contains only Dual-specific orchestration fields. This aligns with the devcontainer ecosystem — users define their container in devcontainer.json, and `.dual.toml` handles only what devcontainer can't (command routing, shared files, volume isolation).

**Breaking change**: Fields `image`, `ports`, `setup`, `env` are removed from `.dual.toml`. Users must move container config to `devcontainer.json`.

## New Config Model

**`.dual.toml`** (Dual-specific only):
```toml
# devcontainer = ".devcontainer/devcontainer.json"  # auto-detects if omitted
extra_commands = ["cargo", "go"]
anonymous_volumes = ["node_modules", ".next"]
[shared]
files = [".env.local"]
```

**`devcontainer.json`** (container config):
```json
{
    "image": "node:20",
    "forwardPorts": [3000],
    "postCreateCommand": "pnpm install",
    "containerEnv": { "NODE_ENV": "development" }
}
```

**Loading flow**: `.dual.toml` (DualConfig) + `devcontainer.json` (DevcontainerJson) → merged `RepoHints`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Clone)]
pub struct DualConfig {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub devcontainer: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub extra_commands: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default = "default_anonymous_volumes")]
    pub anonymous_volumes: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub shared: Option<SharedConfig>,
}
```

`RepoHints` stays unchanged — it's the internal merged representation all consumers use.

1. `load_dual_config()` — reads `.dual.toml` → `DualConfig` (defaults if missing)

- `write_default_devcontainer()` — writes `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` with `{"image": "node:20"}` (valid JSON, no comments)

### 1d. Add `write_dual_config()` and `parse_dual_config()` helpers

For tests. Keep old `write_hints()`/`parse_hints()` temporarily but mark unused.

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` clean
